newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bad quality, high leu hit Romania export-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Bad quality, high leu hit Romania export-analysts.

text.p: An artificially high exchange rate, high industrial costs and slack demand for Romanian products has triggered a plunge in exports, analysts said on Wednesday.
National Statistics Board data showed exports, the main hard currency earner, sank by 16.1 percent to $575.8 million in July, reversing the previous month's rise of 10.3 percent.
The Board's report said direct exports fell as a percentage of industrial output in most sectors with access to European Union (EU) markets, such as clothing, furniture and metallurgy.
Some 53 percent of Romania's seven-month exports went to EU countries, the report said.
Because exports usually pick-up in the summer, July's drop will be a blow to efforts to stockpile hard currency needed to fund winter fuel imports.
The Statistics Board also said lower imports in July had affected the economy, generating "an unfavourable impact on the supply of raw materials, energy and capital goods."
Independent analyst Ilie Serbanescu said "Romania's current industry does not have the strength to penetrate western markets.
"The same production structures will always yield the same exportable goods and for the time being, we don't have very attractive goods," he said.

Romania has done little to reform inefficient industries, inherited from communism, in which armies of workers produce goods that few want. Stored products at end-July were 65.9 percent of the month's output.
Government measures to keep the local leu currency artifically high and ward off inflation ahead of November polls also badly damaged industrial competitiveness, analysts said.

The leu has slipped only gradually over recent months, discouraging exporters. On Wednesday, the leu was quoted at 3,155/65 against the dollar on the local interbank market while more realistic retail prices hovered around 3,550. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
